clue.text: Fool somehow atoning accepting one mission

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: accepting means the rearranged letters take a piece in among them
somehow says these letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone tells a fool that making amends somehow involves taking on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' shuffles the letters, and 'accepting' takes I inside them to make IGNATION. 'Mission' here means an assigned task rather than a secret meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignation can mean an assignment or allotted task, close to a mission given to someone.

clue.text: Belt a girl or boy

parts.note: a sash is a belt or band worn round the waist

explanation.surface: A belt is offered to either a girl or a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasha is a given name used for both sexes, a Russian pet form of Alexander or Alexandra.

clue.text: Take cover according to report not going far out to sea

definitions.text: not going far out to sea

indicators.note: according to report means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to take out cover against loss is to insure

explanation.surface: A sailor takes cover by staying close to the coast, so the report says.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore describes fishing or sailing kept close to the coast, not venturing far out.

clue.text: Relative from Newcastle area that was close!

parts.note: Newcastle is in North-East England, abbreviated NE
phew is the exclamation of relief after a near miss

explanation.surface: A relative from Tyneside breathes a sigh of relief after a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew, a sibling's son, is a family relation.

clue.text: Fighter in ring moved fast put on deck endlessly

parts.note: tore means rushed or moved fast

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the decorating word is dropped

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or decorate

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring dashed about and was then decked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter in ring' suggests a boxer; the ring is a bullring. 'Deck' here means decorate, not knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, who fights in the bullring.

clue.text: One caught in bid to be policeman perhaps

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the word for bid

parts.note: a bid is an offer
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught bidding to become a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is one kind of officer; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: One responsible for girls resolving mothers' issues

indicators.note: resolving means breaking down and reworking the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A teacher in charge of girls sorts out problems raised by their mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolving' rearranges MOTHERS and ISSUES. A housemistress runs a boarding house in a British girls' school.
explanation.definitionFit: In a boarding school the housemistress has charge of the pupils in her house.

clue.text: Hero's declaration to partner Bush

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Hero's lover was Leander
a bush or shrub, the evergreen with pink flowers

explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a poisonous evergreen flowering shrub, so a kind of bush.

clue.text: Not getting on with inferior types

definitions.meaning: family members who are poor and do not get on well, i.e. relatives in a bad way
those regarded as a weaker or lesser version of something

explanation.definitionFit: Poor relations are lesser examples of a type, and literally kin who are not prospering.

clue.text: Restful place, old, unaltered

parts.note: as is means unchanged, left in its current state

explanation.surface: An old resting spot has been left exactly as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a place of calm and refreshment.

clue.text: Left paper behind — minister's responsible for it

indicators.note: behind places the paper after the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a folio is a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A minister leaves papers behind, papers he is responsible for.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the government department or brief they hold.

clue.text: TV programme like this — a frivolously entertaining time

parts.note: so means thus, like this
pop describes light popular entertainment
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A TV show of this kind offers a lightly entertaining time.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television.

clue.text: Toast introducing one person in charge

indicators.note: introducing means one piece is brought into another

parts.note: to char is to scorch or toast
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to introduce the person presiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' suggests a drink to the chairman; it is the verb to char.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair is the person presiding over a meeting.

clue.text: Having power in two-wheeler cleaned up

indicators.note: in means the letter for power goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a moped is a small motorised two-wheeler
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A powered two-wheeler was given a wipe down.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up spillage is to clean it away; mopped means wiped clean.

clue.text: Insect invades ordinary weed

indicators.note: invades means the insect gets inside the other word

parts.note: plain means ordinary or simple
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect invades a common weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain is a common lawn weed of the genus Plantago.

clue.text: Leaders of persistent offenders robbing bank — get this?

indicators.note: leaders are the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: a ridge is a raised bank of earth

explanation.surface: Repeat criminals who rob a bank: guess what they get?
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which is what such offenders get.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge is British slang for serving time in prison, the reward bank robbers receive.

clue.text: Colour used by Lear to write about match

indicators.note: about means the writing word goes around the matching word

parts.note: to pen is to write
to agree is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: Lear writes about a colour to suit his match.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's poem has the Owl and the Pussy-cat sailing in a pea-green boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea-green is a yellowish green, the colour of Lear's boat in The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Mum strolls along in a muddle

parts.note: mum as in keeping mum means be quiet, sh
ambles means walks slowly

explanation.surface: Mother wanders about in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother; it means silence, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles is a state of total disorder or confusion.

clue.text: Polish get-togethers grow bigger

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering, like a sewing bee
the moon waxes, growing larger

explanation.surface: Polish gatherings keep expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality; it is the noun for a shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswax is used to make furniture polish.

clue.text: Guide with turn of phrase

indicators.note: a turn of the letters rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A guide has a clever turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters.

clue.text: Environment's not much in Derby perhaps

indicators.note: in means the small amount sits inside the headgear

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat, so an example of a hat
a bit means a small amount

explanation.surface: The surroundings of Derby are not up to much.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city; it is the American name for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where an organism lives.

clue.text: City trader more hard-up

definitions.meaning: a dealer in the City of London's financial markets
comparative of broke, having less money

explanation.definitionFit: A broker buys and sells shares; 'broke' means penniless, so the comparative is more hard-up.

clue.text: Even priest-like characters join again

indicators.note: even here asks for the even-numbered letters only, with characters as the link to them

explanation.surface: Even priest-like characters get married again.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to tie or fasten together once more.

clue.text: A coarse fellow held by soldier, revolutionary leader

indicators.note: held by means the following pieces sit inside the soldier

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a ribald is an archaic word for a coarse, vulgar person

explanation.surface: A rough character is captured by a soldier who leads a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the revolutionary campaign to unify Italy.

clue.text: Pick up pound on merit

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling
to earn is to merit or deserve

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a pound on merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill is to learn it.

clue.text: Whisper surreptitiously about end of Bismarck — as this?

indicators.note: surreptitiously suggests the letters are moved about stealthily

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: People whisper secretly about the fate of the battleship Bismarck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bismarck was a German battleship sunk in 1941, ending up as the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken battleship such as the Bismarck is a wreck, the result of a vessel being lost.

clue.text: Teach several things in succession

definitions.meaning: a series or chain of linked events

explanation.definitionFit: To train is to teach a skill; a train of events or thought is a connected sequence.

clue.text: Pardoning unruly Generation X

indicators.note: unruly means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disorderly Generation X are being forgiven.
explanation.definitionFit: Exonerating means clearing someone of blame, absolving them.
